title: Northern Lakes Business Office orientation.

steps.text: Today is the operating dashboard for what needs attention now.
Customers keeps customer records, properties, history, and Customer 360 together.
Jobs and Work holds active service, assignments, task status, and closeout.
Meetings captures decisions, notes, and follow-up in business context.
Quotes is where approved scope becomes customer-ready pricing and revision history.
Schedule is for dispatch, timing, recurring occurrences, and calendar review.
Messages keeps customer and team communication connected to the work.
Site Visit captures property conditions, measurements, photos, and proof.
Billing handles invoices, balances, receipts, expenses, and payment status.
Accounting organizes the native financial record for review and handoff.
Payroll Prep gathers employee and work records needed for payroll preparation.
Tax Prep packages records for review and export; it does not automatically file taxes.
Reports shows receivables, profitability, service performance, and operating trends.
People manages employees, site managers, role access, and assignments.
Inventory tracks service materials, parts, and consumables when those records are used.
Fleet keeps trucks, skid steers, mowers, trailers, and other equipment organized.
Documents stores photos, PDFs, receipts, reports, and other connected files.
Controls holds approval boundaries, proof, and safeguards.
The Assistant helps review and prepare work while keeping changes behind owner approval.
Settings holds Northern Lakes business configuration and tenant-specific options.

title: Capture a meeting and turn it into organized follow-up.

steps.text: Start in Meetings. Link the meeting to the correct customer or job when that context exists, then capture decisions, notes, and action items.
Return to Customer 360 when the meeting belongs to a customer so the conversation stays in the same operating history.
Create or confirm the follow-up task or job action in Work instead of leaving an important commitment only in meeting notes.
Store the meeting report, approved recording, photos, or supporting documents with the related business record. Review before printing or sharing.

title: Use a Northern Lakes Site Visit to build a defensible quote.

steps.text: Open the correct customer and property before the site visit so evidence cannot land on the wrong record.
Capture measurements, photos, access conditions, obstacles, scope notes, and equipment needs while you are at the property.
Build the quote from the verified site evidence. Check quantities, rates, service wording, and special requirements before preparing the customer document.
Keep the supporting photos and files connected to the same customer, property, Site Visit, and quote for later review.

title: Revise a Northern Lakes quote without losing the original scope.

steps.text: Open the existing quote instead of creating a disconnected replacement. Review the current scope, measurements, service lines, quantities, and rates.
Make the approved revision, regenerate the customer-ready version, and review the changed wording and total before delivery.
The Assistant may help review or prepare a revision, but data-changing actions stay behind owner approval.
After the customer accepts the revised scope, make sure the job reflects the accepted version so operations and billing do not use an outdated quote.

title: Manage Northern Lakes users, settings, and approval controls.

steps.text: Use People to add or review employees, site managers, and other approved users by exact email and role. Never share owner credentials.
Use Settings for Northern Lakes business identity, service configuration, recurring-service rules, and tenant-specific options.
Controls defines the actions that need approval and provides proof and recovery boundaries for sensitive work.
When an assistant proposes a tenant-data change, review the preview and approve only the intended change. Shared engine changes remain suggestions.

title: Northern Lakes owner money workspace overview.

steps.text: Start in Billing to review money in, money out, unpaid invoices, receipts, expenses, and payment status. This is the operational money view, not an automatic payment system.
Move to Accounting to review how invoices, expenses, deposits, vendor obligations, and reconciled activity become the native financial record.
Use Reports to connect daily transactions to receivables, payables, profitability, cash position, and owner follow-up.

title: Enter, review, and approve a vendor bill.

steps.text: Enter the vendor bill with the verified vendor, invoice date, due date, amount, category, job or overhead context, and supporting document.
Review the bill in the accounting record so duplicate bills, incorrect coding, or missing job context are caught before payment preparation.
Owner approval is the payment boundary. The system can identify what is due and prepare the next action, but it does not silently pay the vendor.

title: Prepare a check or electronic vendor payment safely.

steps.text: Open the approved payable and verify vendor, amount, due date, payment method, and the bill being satisfied.
Use the accounting record to confirm the payment will be applied to the correct payable and will not create a duplicate expense.
The Office may tell the owner what check to write or what approved payment to send. Final payment execution remains an owner-controlled external action.

title: Handle customer deposits, credits, and refund review.

steps.text: Record a customer deposit against the correct customer, quote, job, or invoice so the remaining balance stays accurate.
Review credits and adjustments in Accounting so the customer balance and financial record agree.
Refunds are sensitive external money actions. Prepare the refund for owner review and approval; do not issue it automatically during normal Office automation.

title: Reconcile bank activity against the Office record.

steps.text: Begin with posted bank activity and the matching Office transactions. Reconciliation confirms what actually cleared instead of assuming an invoice or bill status is correct.
Investigate unmatched deposits, payments, fees, transfers, and expenses from the operational money record.
After reconciliation, review cash and outstanding balances again so reports reflect cleared activity and unresolved items remain visible.

title: Reconcile credit-card activity and missing receipts.

steps.text: Review card purchases and make sure each expense has the correct vendor, date, amount, category, job context, and receipt when available.
Use Documents and Smart Upload to attach missing receipt evidence to the related expense rather than leaving it in a phone gallery or email inbox.
Reconcile the card statement to the expense record and leave unmatched or unsupported transactions in review instead of forcing a false match.

title: Prepare payroll and employee reimbursement review.

steps.text: Confirm the employee record and role before reviewing payroll-related work or reimbursements.
Payroll Prep gathers approved employee and work records for payroll preparation. Verify hours, job context, exceptions, and source evidence before handoff.
Employee reimbursements should reference the actual expense and receipt, with owner review before money is sent.
Payroll execution and reimbursement payments remain protected actions even when Office prepares the supporting record.

title: Use cash-flow scenarios and owner payment review.

steps.text: Review the cash scenario as decision support: expected receivables, bills due, current recorded balances, and timing assumptions.
Open the underlying invoices and payables before acting on a cash recommendation. A scenario is not the same as confirmed available cash.
Use the Assistant to summarize what needs attention or compare options, then verify the source records before approving a payment decision.

title: Review the owner financial report pack.

steps.text: Use the report pack to review profit and loss, balance-sheet style position, accounts receivable aging, accounts payable aging, job profitability, and operating trends supported by the native records.
When a report number looks wrong, return to the source accounting records instead of editing the report output itself.
Use the operational money view to resolve unpaid invoices, bills due, missing receipts, and payment-status issues that drive the reports.

title: Move a lead into a real customer and property record.

steps.text: Treat an inquiry as a lead until identity, contact information, property, and requested service are verified.
When the lead is qualified, create or confirm the canonical customer and property instead of creating duplicates for each request.
If the scope needs site evidence, move directly into Site Visit so measurements, photos, and conditions stay connected to the new customer.
Build the quote from the verified customer, property, and scope rather than copying information into a disconnected estimate.

title: Coordinate customer communication with the customer portal.

steps.text: Keep customer communication attached to the correct customer and work context whenever possible. Review outbound wording before sending.
Customer 360 is the internal history for messages, quotes, work, invoices, files, and approvals.
The customer portal exposes only approved customer-facing information. Internal notes, employee controls, and owner-only financial tools remain separate.

title: Use electronic approval and signature without losing document history.

steps.text: Prepare the customer-ready quote or approval document from the current scope and revision.
Keep the issued document and supporting evidence attached to the same record so the signed version can be compared to what was approved.
Electronic approval or signature records customer intent; it does not bypass owner controls for later pricing changes, refunds, or other protected actions.

title: Create and approve a change order after work has started.

steps.text: When field conditions change the approved scope, document the issue on the existing job instead of silently changing the original agreement.
Capture photos, measurements, notes, or other evidence that explains why the scope changed.
Prepare the revised pricing or change order from the documented difference and review the customer-facing amount and wording.
Keep the changed scope behind the appropriate customer and owner approval before billing it as completed work.

title: Use offline-safe field forms and checklists.

steps.text: Open the assigned work before heading into a weak-signal area so the operator has the correct customer, property, and service context.
Use the configured checklist or field form for required steps, measurements, proof, and issue notes. Keep entries on the same job.
Offline-safe changes may queue for replay. Do not create duplicate jobs or repeat financial actions just because connectivity is slow.
After connectivity returns, confirm the queued work synchronized and the current status is correct before moving on.

title: Use owner intelligence and the Office Assistant for decision support.

steps.text: Run the AI Team scan for advisory findings from this business only. Open a finding and check the actual invoice, job, quote, or customer record behind it. Ask for an owner brief when a summary helps; a scan is not an automatic action.
Use the report and profitability views to inspect the evidence behind the summary rather than treating the assistant response as the accounting record.
For payment or cash decisions, verify the actual invoice, payable, and recorded balance before approving an action.
Assistant plans are preview-first. High-impact actions remain behind owner approval and should leave proof of what was approved.

title: Configure safe automation, approvals, and integrations.

steps.text: Use Controls to review the approval queue and define what Office may prepare automatically versus what always needs owner approval.
Low-impact internal organization can be automated when configured. Sending messages, changing pricing, issuing refunds, paying bills, moving money, or other external actions stay approval-gated.

Use Settings to confirm private Office file storage is active. Client-owned Google Drive is unavailable for this release and must remain gated until separate onboarding and upload acceptance pass. A missing provider never counts as connected.
Integration status should show health and capability without exposing API keys, tokens, or secrets. H38 and Northern Lakes remain isolated tenants on the same shared engine.
